Descriptive statistics chapter

Descriptive statistics: delivery and quality audit

Chapter state

This is a complete English review draft of only s_descriptive, the Week 3 descriptive-statistics chapter. The previous searching-and-selection chapter was explicitly approved before work began. Student approval is still required to promote this chapter and begin the next one.

The deliverable contains 22 lesson sections, 80 independently authored or course-inspired solved problems, two checked authentic examination adaptations, a complete summary, 80 final examination rules, 28 distinct stored statistical models with 198 checkpoints, and 14 editable laboratory modes. Reusing a model inside a worked answer does not create another distinct model; the browser mounts 43 instances.

Inferential estimation, hypothesis tests, detailed sampling distributions and full regression inference are deliberately scoped to their own scheduled chapters. Population variance and normal standardization are explicitly marked bridges in the authentic bank.

Sources and original-PDF inspection

Five universities contribute genuinely reviewed written material: Berkeley, MIT, Stanford, Carnegie Mellon and Harvard. The source audit records ranking criteria, exact reading scopes and convention differences. Oxford was critically examined and not selected as core; ETH was index-screened, not represented as a read lecture. An unavailable guessed Stanford URL was excluded.

The two authentic questions retain the archive commit and verified original-file SHA-256: PhD CS 1405 Q58 on PDF page 15 and MS CE 1405 Q36 on PDF page 8. Their printed option order was checked visually. Answers 3 and 1 respectively are independently derived, not claimed official keys. The scanned archive was not exhaustively read or classified in this chapter.

Mathematics and code verification

The audit runner performed 59 exact named arithmetic checks using rational arithmetic, including inverse-summary roots, weighting, strict-tail constructions, grouped approximations, pooling, the zero-third-moment counterexample, tied Spearman ranks, original-PDF hashes and original answers. It also enumerated 775 small finite lists to check the single-residual/range bounds and exact append identities. These checks supplement the written proofs rather than replace them.

The real JavaScript generators were compared against separate finite reference calculations in 1,440 seeded algorithm-comparison groups. Checks covered histogram endpoints and areas, ECDF ties and left limits, quantile interpolation, variance/Welford, affine scaling, boxplot fences/whiskers, pooling, correlation, moving-average startup, EWMA expansion and loss minimizers. All 28 stored models retain exact snapshots, explanations, predicates and changed fields.

Semantic review corrected a false draft skewness construction before delivery, proved attainability for both tail conventions in original problem 52, corrected the fence-equal whisker reasoning in problem 41, and separated empirical correlation from population independence in problem 72. The lesson and final rules reflect these corrections consistently. Floating-point laboratory results remain finite-precision computations; exact rational examples provide their reference.

Fonts, formulas, diagrams and real browser controls

The actual chapter was rendered in Edge. All 198 stored model checkpoints were inspected by geometric checks: no reported text overlap, clipping or label-padding defect. Statistical plot polygons and axes retain their mathematical coordinates; they are not converted into graph-node connectors. Histogram density and bin endpoints use actual coordinates, loss curves use a labelled loss axis, and paired/time/Q–Q plots show their numerical scale.

Native MathML contains structured fractions, sums and scripts, with STIX Two Math separate from Source Sans 3 prose and Newsreader headings. JetBrains Mono is loaded for code. No raw TeX delimiter, Persian text or underlined link remains in the chapter. Font files loaded successfully and no hidden MathML block was reported when solutions were opened.

Actual controls were exercised: play, exact pause/resume, previous, seek and restart; reduced-motion mode suppresses movement; printing exposes explanatory checkpoints. All 14 editable modes returned their checked results. Five invalid-input cases preserve the prior valid laboratory. A 390-pixel viewport has no page-level horizontal overflow; wide plots have their own scroll region. Runtime errors were absent.

Rendered screenshots of histogram, boxplot, streaming, loss, correlation, title and mobile layout are retained alongside the browser report. They were visually inspected for readability and mathematical placement. Geometry checks and finite screenshots do not prove every possible user-entered layout perfect.

Prior-library preservation and review gate

All 38 preceding chapter HTML hashes are unchanged. This retains all 2,346 preceding complete problem bodies. Only the approved status of a_select, the new chapter metadata and active-delivery evidence change. The resulting library contains 39 chapter pages and 2,428 complete problems. Synced project sources/ remain untouched.

Detailed evidence files are in research/s_descriptive-evidence: reading.json, mathematics.json, models.json, browser.json and lesson-and-retention.json. GitHub mirroring and private publication are recorded only after their actual verification in the separate publication receipt. Unrelated archive deletions in the mirror are preserved.

No finite source pool, proof review or test suite guarantees literal universal correctness or performance on every unseen question. This draft makes its scope and remaining uncertainty explicit and awaits the student's review.
